issues.quote: I walk in the cold when I want to think, and I was thinking about the repeater.
issues.fact: B2 says Girard went out at 10:21 by his watch and stayed under the front windows of the house. Nothing says he moved away from that spot.
issues.misreading: 'I walk in the cold' suggests he was walking about the street during the interval, so a solver could conclude he was not under the front windows for the whole period from 10:21 to 10:46 and could have been elsewhere.

issues.quote: What did I take them for? A repeater, I would have said. In my trade you know the sound.
issues.fact: B4 says only that he heard faint quick bells from the master's window at 26 minutes to eleven by his watch. The sheet does not say what made the sound.
issues.misreading: Identifying the bells as a repeater suggests a watch striking, which a solver could read as a clue about whose watch or timepiece was sounding, and so as a hint beyond the stated reading.

issues.quote: Monnier had made us all show our watches, as he does every year, and told me my case wanted cleaning and my hands were a disgrace.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about the accuracy or synchronisation of any watch. Girard's readings are simply 'by my watch'.
issues.misreading: Mention of a watch-showing ritual, followed by 'A merchant notices time... It is what we sell', could lead a solver to assume Girard's watch was checked and accurate, which the sheet does not establish.
